person: Rosa Villanueva is 64, a retired school cafeteria manager in Texas. She keeps a folder of papers for each property: the house, the duplex and the lot. She hears from a mailer that she may be paying mortgage insurance she no longer owes, and she wants it checked loan by loan. Her husband says to just pay what the bank asks, but she wants to know what is actually owed. She also handles the loan of her widowed mother, Elena, under a power of attorney. She is wary of the paid removal services and of anything that wants her bank login. Her tech comfort is low, and she wants the deadline first and plain words.
stated_up_front: I think we're still paying mortgage insurance on the house and my mother's loan and maybe shouldn't be. I have the papers right here, so tell me which one you want and I'll read you the number. Please don't make me pay somebody to do this.

facts.about: The house: purchase price on the closing disclosure
facts.truth: $240,000 in June 2020, with 8% down. The loan was $220,800.

facts.about: The house: appraisal shown on the servicer's page
facts.truth: $252,000. The sale price is the lower figure, so $240,000 is the original value, and 80% of it is $192,000.

facts.about: The house: current balance and extra payments
facts.truth: The balance is $189,400. She has sent about $12,000 of extra principal since 2023, mostly $500 a month.

facts.about: The house: extra payment left unapplied
facts.truth: A $4,000 lump sum sent in March 2026 shows as 'unapplied funds' at the servicer and was never put on the principal.
No late payments in the last two years. One payment in 2022 was 16 days late and carried a late fee.
A contractor's lien from a 2022 roof job was released in 2024. No other second lien.
Original value $130,000. The schedule reached 78% ($101,400) in March 2026. Premiums of $71 a month were still charged from April to October 2026.
The May 2026 payment was 52 days late because of a hospital stay. The payment history before March was clean.
A home equity line on the duplex was paid off and closed in 2023. A lot loan was paid in full in 2021. Neither has mortgage insurance.
A $399 'PMI removal' company wants her to sign up. An email from 'Lonestar Home Loans Support' asks for her online banking password.

unknowns: Whether the house's mortgage insurance can be cancelled now, or only on the loan's schedule
What date the law says the insurance on her mother's loan had to end
What 'unapplied funds' means and why the servicer holds the $4,000 instead of applying it
Whether the 52-day late payment on her mother's loan changes anything for the earlier charges
